title: Bounded interactive Site runtime activation
opportunity: After a Site write committed, POST/PUT/DELETE activated the runtime from a fresh PostgreSQL snapshot using the request token directly.
rootCause: A slow activation snapshot could delay the interactive mutation response after PostgreSQL had already committed, without distinguishing runtime-refresh timeout from database write failure.
implementation: Added a two-second linked SiteRuntimeActivationBudget with explicit client-cancellation distinction.
Applied it to interactive create, update and delete runtime activation while preserving the existing lock, validation-read and write boundaries.
Returned site_runtime_activation_timeout with a safe message stating that PostgreSQL was written but runtime refresh exceeded its limit, and added Thai browser recovery copy.

tdd.red: SiteRuntimeActivationBudgetTests initially failed to compile because the activation budget policy did not exist; the endpoint contract then failed until all three mutation paths used the budget.

verification.impeccableDetector: 0 anti-patterns; four pre-existing advisory design-system-color findings in app.js (#ff4d5e, #22374f, #ff6378); no new finding

boundaries: Live PostgreSQL slow-activation execution, authenticated browser/published-EXE smoke, visual responsive verification, full VSTest testhost connectivity, CodeQL/SARIF, external penetration testing, load/SLO, SIEM, Authenticode signing, and production certification remain unverified.
